summary: The S&P 500 fell 0.22% today to 7,660, giving back some of yesterday's gains as investors sat on their hands waiting for Nvidia earnings after the close. The Fed's preferred inflation measure, called core PCE, came in at 0.2% for the month and 3.3% annually according to press coverage, which is still well above the Fed's 2% target and suggests interest rates will stay higher for longer. Oil rose 0.74% to $82.97 and energy stocks were the best sector today, up 1.08%. Tomorrow brings Canadian bank earnings from CM.TO and RY.TO, plus unemployment claims, and Friday brings a speech from Fed Chair Warsh.
